title: Code Quality and Test Architecture
outOfScope: Product feature behavior unrelated to governance tooling.
A complete rewrite of every existing large script.
Provider, adopter, release publication, and Japanese capability assessment work reserved for later Work Items.
Changing archived evidence or deleting tests, snapshots, or Work Items.

sources.reason: WI-12 scope, acceptance, and required verification.
Current quality, lint, type, coverage, and project test entry points.
Governance implementation surface to classify and guard.
Existing test layers and negative regression coverage.

riskAssessment.reason: Quality architecture changes can weaken fail-closed governance if the new classification or safety checks are incomplete.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized serial execution of the remediation plan; this Work Item is bounded to quality architecture and regression guards.

preReviewWarnings: Confirm new checks do not claim complete safety or replace human review.
Confirm the test architecture records unsupported layers as not applicable rather than silently passing.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A deterministic quality-architecture checker classifies project test layers and fails closed on unsafe subprocess/path patterns.
The checker has unit and negative regression coverage, including shell metacharacters, path traversal, symlink, encoding, and mutable-default cases.
The test architecture and checks catalog document required layers, evidence expectations, and not-applicable handling without overstating coverage.
Ruff, mypy, focused tests, full project checks, coverage, security, installer, release, and governance checks pass or are explicitly recorded with reasons.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Preserve fail-closed behavior and keep path/subprocess handling explicit and auditable.
Do not turn test or static-analysis results into claims about provider or production controls.

intent.problem: The repository has many governance scripts and test files, but the required test layers and safety invariants are not represented by one deterministic, reviewable architecture contract.
constraints: Keep the implementation bounded; do not rewrite all existing scripts.
Use standard-library deterministic checks where possible.
Maintain current 85 percent coverage and existing governance gates.
Do not imply that local checks verify external enterprise controls.
intent.rationale: A small architecture checker and explicit test matrix make quality boundaries executable while preserving the existing lifecycle and later Japanese/release gates.

rawUserRequest: Execute the approved AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation plan serially. For WI-12, modularize and harden quality/test architecture within scope, run the complete Work Item/PR/merge/close workflow, record issues, and align documentation before the next Work Item.

declaredIntent.summary: Harden the repository's executable quality and test architecture within the bounded WI-12 scope.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Unsafe command and path patterns are rejected.
Explicit argv and repository-relative paths are accepted.
Unavailable test layers are recorded as not applicable.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Explicit user authorization to execute the approved remediation plan and update governed documentation/evidence.
